'''Michael Handel''' is an American mathematician known for his work in [[Geometric group theory]]. He is a professor in the Department of Mathematics at [[Lehman College]] of the [[City University of New York]] and a professor of mathematics at the [[CUNY Graduate Center]].

==Career==
Michael Handel graduated with a B.A. in mathematics from [[Brandeis University]] in 1971.<ref name=ias1>{{cite web|url=https://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/annualreportforf1984inst.pdf|title=Institute for Advanced Study Annual Report 1984|accessdate=August 18, 2020}}</ref>{{nbsp}} He received his Ph.D. from [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1975 under the supervision of [[Robion Kirby]].<ref name=genealogy>{{MathGenealogy|id=23943|title=Michael Handel|accessdate=August 14, 2020}}</ref>{{nbsp}} From 1975 to 1978, he was an instructor at [[Princeton University]]. He joined the faculty of [[Michigan State University]] as an assistant professor in 1978,<ref name=msu1>{{cite web|url=http://spartanhistory.kora.matrix.msu.edu/files/3/15/3-F-1C3-56-SEPTEMBER%2021-22%201978.pdf|title=Michigan State Spartan History|date=September 21, 1978|accessdate=August 18, 2020}}</ref>{{nbsp}} and was promoted to associate professor in 1983.<ref name=msu2>{{cite web|url=http://spartanhistory.kora.matrix.msu.edu/files/3/15/3-F-338-56-MAY%2026-27%201983.pdf|title=Michigan State Spartan History|date=May 26, 1983|accessdate=August 18, 2020}}</ref>{{nbsp}} Handel was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1978 to 1979, and again from 1987 to 1988.<ref name=ias>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/michael-handel|title=Michael Handel at the Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|accessdate=August 14, 2020}}</ref>{{nbsp}} In 1990, he joined the Mathematics Department at Lehman College.

Handel is best known for developing the [[Train track map]] method in [[Geometric group theory]] in collaboration with [[Mladen Bestvina]] in 1992.<ref name="BH01">Mladen Bestvina, and Michael Handel, [https://www.jstor.org/pss/2946562 ''Train tracks and automorphisms of free groups.''] [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), volume 135 (1992), number 1, pages 1–51</ref>{{nbsp}} Bestvina, Feighn and Handel later proved that the group Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'') satisfies the [[Tits alternative]], settling a long-standing open problem.<ref name="BFH00">Mladen Bestvina, Mark Feighn, and Michael Handel. [http://www.emis.de/journals/Annals/151_2/bestvina.pdf ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). I. Dynamics of exponentially-growing automorphisms.''] [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), volume 151 (2000), number 2, pages 517–623</ref><ref name="BFH05">Mladen Bestvina, Mark Feighn, and Michael Handel.  [http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/2005/161-1/p01.xhtml ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). II. A Kolchin type theorem.''] [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), volume 161 (2005), number 1, pages 1–59</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*In 1984, Handel won a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref name=sloan>{{cite web|url=https://sloan.org/past-Fellows?page=382|title=Past Sloan Fellows|accessdate=August 14, 2020}}</ref>
*In 2014, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=ams>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#h|title= Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|accessdate=August 14, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gc.cuny.edu/Page-Elements/Academics-Research-Centers-Initiatives/Doctoral-Programs/Mathematics/Program-News/Detail?id=21757|title= Two GC Professors Named Fellows of the American Mathematical Society for 2014|accessdate=August 14, 2020}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Handel, Michael. "One Dimensional Minimal Sets and the Seifert Conjecture ". ''[[Annals of Mathematics]] (2)'' 111 (1980), number 1, pages 35–66. [http://doi.org/10.2307/1971216 DOI:10.2307/1971216]
*Feighn, Mark; Handel, Michael. "Mapping tori of free group automorphisms are coherent". ''[[Annals of Mathematics]] (2)'' 149 (1999), number 3, pages 1061–1077. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=1709311 MR 1709311]
*Bestvina, Mladen; Feighn, Mark; Handel, Michael. [http://www.emis.de/journals/Annals/151_2/bestvina.pdf ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). I. Dynamics of exponentially-growing automorphisms.''] [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), volume 151 (2000), number 2, pages 517–623
*Bestvina, Mladen; Feighn, Mark; Handel, Michael.  [http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/2005/161-1/p01.xhtml ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). II. A Kolchin type theorem.''] [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), volume 161 (2005), number 1, pages 1–59 [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=2150382 MR 2150382]
*Handel, Michael; Mosher, Lee. "The free splitting complex of a free group, I: hyperbolicity". ''[[Geometry & Topology]]'' 17 (2013), number 3, pages 1581–1672. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=3073931 MR 3073931]
